newsitem.title: UK: British March PEP sales jump to fresh record.
newsitem.headline: British March PEP sales jump to fresh record.

text.p: British Personal Equity Plan (PEP) sales jumped in March to a fresh record and remained strong in early April to dispel gloomy forecasts for the industry.
The Association of Unit Trusts and Investment Funds (AUTIF) said on Monday net unit trust PEP sales in March were 1.14 billion sterling ($1.9 billion), up 56 million on April 1996's previous record.

Sales in early April before the end of the tax year on April 5 were 797 million, bringing total net PEP sales for the 1996/7 tax year to 6.2 billion sterling, up some 43 percent on the previous tax year's 4.3 billion.

Disappointing sales figures earlier in the year had raised fears that a high spending advertising campaign by industry members would fall flat despite a strong play on tax uncertainty ahead of an expected Labour election victory.
But industry players reported a strong rise in interest in the closing days of the tax year.
Labour has said that it would extend the principle of PEPs to encourage long-term saving if it came to power.
AUTIF said sales in March were on a par with sales for the whole of 1992.
Sales in March were dominated by the two UK growth sectors, UK Growth and UK Growth and Income. Each of these took 20 percent of the 1.1 billion sterling total.
The Association said the total value of unit trust funds had risen to 140.6 billion sterling by end-March, and PEP funds to 27.9 billion against 19.4 billion a year earlier.
The figures cover PEP plans operated by unit trust managers only and not plans operated by all PEP plan managers.
- Andrew Gill, London newsroom +171 542 5887 ($ = 0.616 British Pounds Sterling)
